title: Inactive replica of new primary shard is green

timeline.message: Inactive replica of new primary shard is green
timeline.author: gmarouli

timeline.body:
When we have a new initialisation of a primary shard we consider the this indicator `green` based on the idea that this are unexceptional events in the cluster's lifecycle. However, when we have a replica of this shard that is inactive we turn to `yellow`. 

With this PR, we change this behaviour to signal that if the primary is inactive and that is `green`, then an inactive replica of this shard is also `green`.

Fixes #99951

timeline.body:
I do not think this resolves the issue completely. Imagine the following example:
```
my-index 0 p STARTED
my-index 0 r INITIALIZING 
```
This can happen in 2 cases:
* a primary of new index just started and corresponding replica is initializing for the first time (should *not* degrade health)
* a node containing replica unexpectedly left cluster and after allocation delay has passed we begin to initialize a new replica from scratch (should degrade health)

Similar with
```
my-index 0 p STARTED
my-index 0 r UNASSIGNED
```

reply.body:
I think it is okay to merge this change as is as long as this does not close the issue and a followup is open to handle above mentioned case. 

Possibly we might use unassignedInfo.reason/unassignedInfo.lastAllocationStatus to distinguish above scenarios but this is not immediately obvious for me at now

Let's examine this case by case, I do not think all of them should be covered here. 

> a primary of new index just started and corresponding replica is initialising for the first time (should not degrade health)

This is true, but then we need to distinguish between creating and just initialising from other reasons. Because currently, initialising replicas for other reasons are meant to be `yellow` the same way that initialising primaries turn `red`. Is my thinking clear?
Ignore my comment above, I missed the **not**.... Let me read more carefully and come back with ideas.

Correct, the issue that I see is following:

| primary      | replica      | status                                |
|--------------|--------------|---------------------------------------|
| unassigned   | unassigned   | green (was yellow before this change) |
| initializing | unassigned   | green (was yellow before this change) |
| started      | unassigned   | yellow                                |
| started      | initializing | yellow                                |
| started      | started      | green                                 |

With this change the health would still change to yellow during index creation even though for a shorter period of time.

I agree that it would really help to have a clear indication that the shard is initializing for the first time especially as replicas are always initializing the same way.

Ok, so in order to separate these cases, we need to know that the primary just `STARTED`, but without keeping history, I do not think we can do that right?

If indeed history is necessary, then we would have to accept for now at least, that this is something we cannot distinguish, and momentarily we might get a yellow status. Do you agree?

I think this change is improvement over what we have already so it makes sense to merge.
But please keep the issue open in case we could solve the issue with initializing replicas in a followup

Thanks for the conversation Ievgen and Mary. ++ on what has been said and advised so far. 

Just out of curiosity, do we require a history in any of the remaining cases? 

Say we have:
```
my-index 0 p STARTED
my-index 0 r INITIALIZING
```
Does it matter if the primay _just_ started or has been started for a while?

@andreidan , we might want to differentiate between a replica that for lost and it's recovering and a replica that is starting up for the first time either because the user created an index or increased the number of replicas. The second one could be thought of that there is no impact since we just now requested the change while the first one could be indicating a problem if the replica was lost because of an issue.

++ that makes sense thanks Mary 

Note that we do have support for looking at `unassignedInfo` when evaluating health however, we only do so in verbose mode as it's a rather expensive operation, especially in the many-shards scenario.

timeline.body: LGTM, thanks for fixing this Mary
